tasks.title: Add PerLinearFt RateType (prerequisite for pricing trim/wall-linear)
tasks.notes: RateType enum missing per_linear_ft. Wire through LineItemFactory + seed a trim LaborRate. Gates t48 (price seeded takeoff lines by kind/trade).

prep.what: Add a `per_linear_ft` case to the `RateType` enum and wire it through the factory and seeder so trim/wall-linear takeoff measurements can receive a priced LaborRate.
prep.understand: `RateType` drives how `LineItemFactory::unitFromRateType()` picks the unit string and how the estimate editor renders rate. Without a linear-foot type, LF measurements from the takeoff (trim runs, wall linear feet) can't price at all. This is additive-only — a small enum extension with clear cascade points.
approach: Add `PerLinearFt = 'per_linear_ft'` to `app/Enums/RateType.php` with a display label (e.g. 'Per Linear Foot').
Update `LineItemFactory::unitFromRateType()` to return `'lf'` for `RateType::PerLinearFt`.
Seed a trim LaborRate in `database/seeders/LaborRateSeeder.php` (e.g. trade='trim', rate_type=PerLinearFt, rate_per_unit~$3.50/lf).
Run `php artisan test` to confirm nothing breaks — additive only, expect full suite green.

tasks.title: Derive wall PAINT area (perimeter x height) — the missing painting measurement
tasks.notes: Wall paint SF = perimeter x height. Perimeter is in engine output but TakeoffEstimateSeeder drops geometry. Add wall_height migration + preserve perimeter + emit wall_paint measurement lines.

prep.what: Add a wall-height field to takeoff projects and compute wall paint SF = perimeter x height per room from the engine's polygon data, so painting measurements auto-populate from blueprints.
prep.understand: A 2D plan has no Z-axis — the engine gives floor area and perimeter but no height. Wall paint needs height. The perimeter IS in the engine output (`meta.perimeter` per room) but `TakeoffEstimateSeeder` currently drops all geometry on import. This task adds the height param, stops dropping perimeter, and emits a wall_paint measurement line per room.
approach: Create migration `add_wall_height_ft_to_estimates`: nullable decimal on `estimates` table (default 8.0 ft or null to inherit project config).
In `TakeoffEstimateSeeder.php`, stop dropping geometry — preserve `meta.perimeter` per room from the engine's room response.
Compute `wall_paint_sf = perimeter * wall_height_ft` per room; emit as a `kind='wall_paint'` measurement line item.
Add wall-height input to `resources/js/Pages/Takeoff/Index.vue` (project-level default, optional per-room override in the Review widget).
resources: Engine room response: `meta.perimeter` field (see SERVICE README or takeoff-engine docs)
engine/assemblies.py in takeoff-engine (wall-height reference from t18 work today)

tasks.title: Label lane v2: M3 vision for outlined-text firms + callout-vs-room filtering
tasks.notes: PDFTron firms outline all text (zero readable text for the live lane). M3 tile lane proven in spike (~4.3 min/sheet, costs money). Ship as opt-in 'read labels (AI)' action + callout filtering.

prep.what: Productize the M3 vision tile lane as an opt-in 'read labels (AI)' action for PDFTron firms where all text is outlined, plus filter callout noise (stair arrows, FEC boxes, general notes) from room name matching.
prep.understand: PDFTron exports outline every glyph — the live-text lane reads zero labels on these sheets. The spike (`docs/spike/run_labels_m3tiles.py`) proved M3 tiled vision reads them at ~4.3 min/sheet. Holabird (free-text firm, 92/109 named) confirms the free lane is fine for non-PDFTron plans. The callout noise is confirmed live on Holabird: UP/DN stair arrows, FEC callouts, and multi-sentence note paragraphs all match as room names from the R13 notes.
approach: Review `docs/spike/run_labels_m3tiles.py` — understand tile slicing, M3 API call structure, and how extracted labels are matched back to room polygons.

Productize as opt-in: add a `read_labels_ai` flag on the sheet job, gate behind a `§7a metered-credits` event, and wire the `MINIMAX_AI` key to the VPS `.env` (secrets decision: add to /opt/takeoff-engine/.env same as other keys).
Wire the new lane into `engine/labels.py` alongside the existing free-text lane — host chooses: free (fast) or AI (costs credits, for PDFTron firms).
Build callout-vs-room filter: exclude strings matching confirmed noise patterns (UP/DN arrows, FEC/AHU callout labels, multi-sentence paragraphs) before room-name assignment.
resources: engine/labels.py (existing free-text label lane to extend alongside)
MiniMax AI API docs: api.minimax.io (vision tiles, model MiniMax-VL-01)

tasks.title: Assemblies-per-room — paint/drywall/flooring quantities + wall heights
tasks.notes: assemblies-lite scaffolded in engine/assemblies.py. Full version: room type -> assemblies + formulas + heights (up to 8 quantities, CSI trade libraries). The last pillar before estimator-grade Excel.

prep.what: Build the full assemblies engine: given a room's classification and polygon geometry, compute flooring, wall paint, drywall, and ceiling quantities using wall height, producing estimator-grade line items for the Excel export.
prep.understand: `engine/assemblies.py` is scaffolded from t6 (assemblies-lite, basic SF output only). The full version maps room type to multiple quantity formulas: floor area -> flooring SF; perimeter x height -> wall paint SF + drywall SF; floor area -> ceiling SF; perimeter LF -> optional molding/trim. Wall height is a param (default to a project-level or system default like 9 ft). One classification can produce up to 8 distinct line items for different CSI trade codes.
approach: Read `engine/assemblies.py` fully — map what's scaffolded (stubs) vs. what needs implementing.
Define the room-type to assembly mapping: floor area (from polygon) -> flooring; perimeter x wall_height_ft -> wall paint + drywall; floor area -> ceiling; perimeter LF -> molding/trim.
Add `wall_height_ft` as an optional per-room param — fall back to project-level default, then system default (9.0 ft).
Wire quantities through `build_sheet_takeoff` orchestrator so each trade type appears as its own row/column in the 5-tab Excel export.
resources: docs/PRD §8 Phase 1 (assemblies spec — room type to assembly formulas)
`build_sheet_takeoff` in the service orchestrator (entry point to wire into)
